answer: On a ridge above a river, surveyors keep one umber gauge post driven into the bank: each morning the keeper climbs the ridge, reads the waterline against the umber paint band, and files the number with the hour. A partner at the next post reads the same water an hour later, and the two numbers must agree within one painted mark or both posts lose their standing. A copied name earns nothing without its own climb and its own matching pair. A thousand fake names need a thousand ridge climbs and a thousand river readings, while one keeper tends one post.
